section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch2 — Piaget's Cognitive Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Piaget's term for the overall process by which a child adjusts their cognitive structures to fit environmental demands, encompassing both assimilation and accommodation, is:
explanation: Adaptation is Piaget's umbrella term for assimilation and accommodation working together to fit the environment.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch2 — Piaget's Cognitive Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: The ability to arrange objects in a logical sequence based on a single property, such as lining up sticks from shortest to longest, is called:
explanation: Seriation is a concrete-operational ability — ordering objects along a quantifiable dimension.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch2 — Piaget's Cognitive Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: When shown 6 red beads and 2 blue beads (all wooden), a pre-operational child asked 'are there more red beads or more wooden beads?' typically answers 'more red beads', incorrectly comparing a subclass to the whole class. This reveals a difficulty with:
explanation: Class inclusion — understanding a subclass is necessarily smaller than the whole class — is a concrete-operational achievement.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch2 — Piaget's Cognitive Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A three-year-old uses a banana as a pretend telephone during play. This use of one object to represent another reflects the emergence of:

options.option_text: The symbolic function, characteristic of the pre-operational stage

explanation: The symbolic function marks the transition into the pre-operational stage, enabling pretend play and early language.

section: Child Development & Pedagogy · Ch2 — Piaget's Cognitive Development
subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: A pre-operational child reasons: 'I had a nap, and then it got dark, so my nap made it dark outside.' This faulty particular-to-particular reasoning is called:
explanation: Transductive reasoning links two particular events causally without a general principle — a hallmark limitation of pre-operational thought.
